=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Overall view:** The Seller's cover note describes several items as "addressed", "adequate", "settled" or "not material". Its own Disclosure Letter says otherwise. Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment, Ironquay payment evidence, the bonus funds flow and the incident investigation are all open. The package blends every claim type into one regime. I'd treat it as an opening position, not a balanced package.

The figures below are suggested negotiating positions for the deal team to confirm, not market certainties.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A higher cap, with fundamental, tax, fraud and specific indemnities outside it. Also a practical route to recovery, such as a retention or escrow, because the Seller is a holding vehicle that may distribute proceeds.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 35-50% for general warranties and seek a retention or escrow. 20% may be tolerable only if everything else is carved out and secured.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25k per claim, and a AUD 250k deductible basket (about 1% of price) where only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** A lower de minimis, a smaller basket, and a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once the threshold is passed). Related claims should aggregate.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at about AUD 10k de minimis and a tipping basket of about AUD 120k (0.5%). A deductible basket combined with a high de minimis erodes recoverability for a company of this size.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months, and any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** At least 24 months for general warranties, so two audit cycles are covered. Time limits should apply only where the SPA expressly says so.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24-36 months, and reverse the default so limits apply to general warranty claims only. The "all Claims" default would silently shorten the tax, title and fraud periods.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Title and capacity warranties get the same cap and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** A separate fundamental regime (title, capacity, solvency, and ideally core IP ownership) capped at 100% of price, with no basket or de minimis. The period should be the longest the law allows (6 years under the NSW contractual limitation period) or longer where permitted.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A title defect goes to the root of the deal, and a AUD 4.8m cap against a AUD 24m price makes no sense for it.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Silent. However, "limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature" would catch fraud.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out for fraud, dishonest concealment and wilful misconduct. It should be uncapped, with no time limit, and exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses should not limit it. It should cover the Seller's knowledge of fraud by the Company.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on it. It is a basic protection, and its absence in a clause that says "any nature" is a significant drafting point.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012 and beyond), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records, as at 5pm 22 September 2026.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, with fair detail. There should be no general data room disclosure, and public searches should be limited to defined ASIC searches. It also needs a bring-down to signing or Completion, with no Seller right to update the disclosures without a Buyer termination right.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general disclosure. The date is also stale (today is 5 Nov 2026), so require an updated letter.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Deletion, and an express clause preserving claims regardless of Buyer knowledge (a "sandbagging" clause). If a concession is needed, limit it to the deal team's actual knowledge of specifically disclosed matters.
- **Recommendation:** Delete. Combined with general disclosure, the "discoverable" limb would let the Seller disclaim virtually every warranty.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, and the condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Buyer should want:** A true condition precedent. Bluefen's consent must be written, unconditional or on terms acceptable to the Buyer, with the DD-002 clause 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. The Buyer should have a termination right and a long-stop date, with the CP waivable only by the Buyer.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the drafting. The Disclosure Letter confirms no consent has been delivered, so "addressed" is wrong. If the Buyer will proceed without it, require a price reduction or deferred consideration tied to retention of Bluefen.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release to be provided after Completion (about AUD 3.2m outstanding).
- **Buyer should want:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free, so the facility should be repaid at Completion out of the proceeds via the funds flow. The Buyer needs a payout letter and signed security releases (PPSR and ASIC) in escrow at Completion. The change-control clause (8.1) should be dealt with as well.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. At minimum, deduct the payout figure from the price and pay the lender directly at Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420k of DD-005 closing bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer should want:** Treatment as a transaction cost or debt-like item, either deducted from the price or paid by the Seller. It should include on-costs: superannuation, NSW payroll tax and workers compensation, as applicable. The Disclosure Letter is silent on these, so confirm.
- **Recommendation:** Require it in the funds flow, with an on-cost estimate to be confirmed with payroll advisers. If the Seller says it is its matter, it should say so in an indemnity.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer should want:** Proof that AUD 180k has been paid (the DD-010 record is not bank verification), plus a confirmatory assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials under DD-004 clause 7.3 as a Completion deliverable. It also wants a broader indemnity for loss from any third-party or Ironquay claim over ownership of the materials. That indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket, with a long claim period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. Until assignment occurs, Paperbark may not own IP it relies on.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material.
- **Buyer should want:** A specific indemnity for all costs and losses, including investigation, notification, regulatory response, remediation and third-party claims. A forensic report should be delivered before Completion, and the Company should make any notifications needed. The indemnity should sit outside the general cap and basket, with a period of at least 3 years. The Buyer should have a say in how the matter is handled.
- **Recommendation:** Require the specific indemnity. About 1,240 records are involved, and the Disclosure Letter says the access, scope and notification questions are all unresolved. If Paperbark is covered by the Privacy Act, the notifiable data breach assessment timeline may already be running. Ask when the Company became aware.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** The renewal terms, including term, termination rights, any prepayments, and whether each has been signed or just proposed. The Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** Request information before conceding. If they are non-cancellable, prepaid or accelerated, treat them as working capital or debt-like items. In any event, add an interim covenant that no renewals are signed without Buyer consent.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime for everything. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims, and limits apply unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate categories, each with its own cap, thresholds and time limits: (1) general warranties; (2) fundamental/title; (3) tax; (4) specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, bonuses); and (5) fraud. Limits on the general category should apply to it only.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure the SPA accordingly. This is the structural fix that resolves several other items.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the Company's own share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: ASIC extracts, share issue and transfer history, the constitution and any shareholder agreement (pre-emption or transfer restrictions), and PPSR searches. These should check for security over the shares, including any Riverlark security, and for options or convertible instruments. Completion deliverables should include signed transfers and waivers. The Disclosure Letter itself says the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Recommendation:** Complete these checks before signing. The Seller's own register is not enough on its own.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:** A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, covering income tax, GST, PAYG, payroll tax and superannuation. It should be capped at 100% of price, with no basket, and run for the amendment period plus a margin (at least 6 years). It needs conduct-of-claims provisions. IP warranties should cover ownership, employee and contractor assignments, no infringement and open-source use, with core IP ownership in the fundamental tier.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled". The Seller has given no tax or IP terms, and the general regime is inadequate for them. Ask for the Seller's proposed tax and IP provisions so the Buyer can mark them up.

---

## Priorities for the mark-up
1. **Structure and carve-outs:** N-014, N-004, N-005 and N-016 (separate regimes, with fraud, tax and fundamental claims outside the general limits).
2. **Neutralise disclosure and knowledge:** N-006 and N-007 (otherwise the warranty package is largely illusory).
3. **Closing mechanics:** N-008 (Bluefen CP), N-009 (Riverlark payout at Completion), N-010 (bonuses in funds flow).
4. **Specific indemnities:** N-011 and N-012.
5. **Further diligence and information requests:** N-013 (Sandbar terms), N-015 (title searches), the Ironquay payment evidence, and the incident forensic status.

I can draft the mark-up language for any of these clauses, or a short issues list to send back to the Seller's counsel, if that would help.
